significance: A small andesite Shaivite temple on an island in Situ Cangkuang lake, 8.5 m tall on a 4.5 m square base, sheltering a 62 cm stone Shiva. Its plain three-stepped roof with pseudo-lingam pinnacles resembles the earliest Central Javanese Hindu temples, and experts put it around the early 8th century, roughly contemporary with the Dieng group.
